name: Supporting Care Leavers at Work
headline: A first job. Can change everything.
intro: Training that helps managers and HR keep care leavers in work without lowering the bar.
glance: 6 hours in person, or 2 hours live online

problem.scene: Day three. An apprentice walks out at lunch.
problem.question: Her manager never finds out why.
without: A sharp reply is taken at face value
with: Managers ask what is going on
A named buddy from day one
problem.standards: Employers who sign the Care Leaver Covenant's Care Leaver Friendly Employer Charter commit to responding with empathy. This course shows managers how.
problem.evidence: It is support without lowering the bar. Managers keep the same expectations and learn the extra support that helps someone meet them.

groups: Supervisors of care leavers, including first-time managers
Council departments and businesses signed up to the Care Leaver Covenant
The named person a new starter can go to
notes: Works well before a new intake

outcomes: Describe what leaving care can mean for someone aged 16 to 25 starting work.
Recognise when housing, money or family pressure is affecting work, and act before a disciplinary.
Use the window of tolerance to explain lateness, shutting down or a sharp reaction to criticism.
Explain why the first 12 weeks matter, and how Radical Candor holds the standard and the relationship.
Plan a 12-week induction and use a feedback script that names the standard and agrees the next step.
Point a care leaver to their personal adviser, the council's offer for care leavers and the £3,000 bursary for apprentices who start under 25.

pillars.title: Four stages of a first job
pillars.stance_line: The same expectations, with the extra support that helps someone meet them.
items: Read what lateness, silence or a sharp reply may be telling you.
A named buddy, the unwritten rules written down and check-ins booked.
Feedback that cares and challenges, and a plan for when a crisis hits.
A progression conversation that agrees one realistic next step.
pillars.base: Built on Siegel's window of tolerance, Baumeister and Leary's need to belong, Kim Scott's Radical Candor and Carol Dweck's work on growth mindset.

story_line: Four stories run through the day: Jess, 18, Bailey, 19, Kayla, 20, and Liam, 21. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on employment for care leavers, including Suffolk County Council, where the induction and supervisor training this course grew from was built for the council's employment programme.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
